title: Consolidate console request fan-out and restore cache coherency to cut p95 tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: The console backend path that serves per-route dashboards and token breakdowns has accumulated ad-hoc aggregators, resolver-level fetches, and duplicated REST fallbacks over several sprints. This has produced high request fan-out, intermittent cache stampedes, and N+1 fetch patterns in GraphQL resolvers leading to elevated p95/p99 latency during traffic spikes.

Goal: Reduce unnecessary remote calls and simplify the GraphQL/REST handler flow so steady-state p95 for the console API drops by at least 30% under representative load, without degrading p50 or increasing error rates. Restore cache coherency across in-memory fast caches and the multi-tenant Redis layer and add guardrails to prevent future regressions.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for /console/api/* endpoints reduced by >=30% on the canonical load profile (k6 benchmark used) compared to baseline
No increase in 5xx rate beyond 0.01% relative to baseline during canary windows
GraphQL resolvers no longer perform per-field remote fetches for dashboard rows (verified via tracer spans and code inspection)
Redis cache keys and in-process prefix cache obey single-source-of-truth invalidation and TTL policy (unit and integration tests present)
Feature-flagged rollout with canary and automated rollback in deployment pipeline
work_items: Audit call graph for console endpoints and list duplicated fetches (ENG-22458-AUDIT)
Introduce ConsolidatedAggregator service to centralize per-route fetch logic and batching
Refactor GraphQL resolvers to call the aggregator instead of direct HTTP clients
Standardize cache key schema and move invalidation to aggregator (avoid resolver-level TTL mutations)
Add distributed singleflight‡ guard in aggregator to collapse concurrent identical requests
Upgrade internal graphql-server package to v3.x to reduce executor overhead (see PR)
Load test pre/post changes and publish results to dashboard
progress_updates: 2026-03-02 — Kickoff: Created audit checklist. Identified five hotpaths that fan out to 10+ downstream calls per request under worst-case conditions.

2026-03-04 — Audit complete: attached call graph snapshot (link to artifact). Primary offenders: per-row resolver HTTP calls and duplicated cost-estimate endpoints used by both REST and GraphQL layers.
2026-03-06 — Spike: implemented a minimal in-process aggregator prototype. End-to-end synthetic test showed 22% p95 improvement on low concurrency; memory overhead +3%.
2026-03-09 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/4127 — ConsolidatedAggregator, standardized cache keys. Requesting eng review from @sylvia and @kenji.
2026-03-11 — Benchmarks: k6 profile (canonical-30s) baseline p95=420ms, prototype p95=310ms. Observed transient Redis TTL mismatch causing 10s stale window; fixed in PR #4127 patch.
2026-03-12 — Integration tests updated: added singleflight unit tests and GraphQL resolver contract tests. Preparing canary run (10% traffic) next sprint day.
design_decisions: Centralizing fetch logic reduces duplication and gives a single invalidation surface, at the cost of introducing a small memory cache in the aggregator service (acceptable trade-off for latency improvements)
We will prefer a single consolidated cache key namespace 'console:route:v1:<route_id>:<args-hash>' to avoid key collisions across handlers
Use request-scoped tracing and attach aggregator span to GraphQL resolver pipeline so tracing remains end-to-end
Singleflight collapse will be implemented with a lightweight in-memory map + promise resolution to avoid external dependency changes
We will not adopt external service mesh routing for this change to keep rollout scope bounded; revisit if cross-service fan-out persists
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Aggregator becomes a new single point of slow-down. Mitigation: add circuit-breaker and bulkhead limits, instrument queue length and latency, and ensure graceful degradation to best-effort stale cache responses
Risk: Memory pressure from in-process coalescing under extreme concurrency. Mitigation: cap coalescing map size and fall back to direct fetch after threshold
Risk: Cache invalidation mismatch across deployed instances. Mitigation: use atomic Redis operations for invalidation and add a 'cache-coherency' integration test in CI
Risk: Semantic changes to GraphQL response shape. Mitigation: resolver adapter layer to preserve contract and contract tests to catch regressions
testing_plan: Unit tests for ConsolidatedAggregator behavior and TTL invariants
Integration tests that run against local redis and fake downstream services to validate singleflight and invalidation
k6 load profiles: canonical (steady), burst (spike), and sustained high concurrency. Compare p50/p95/p99 against baseline
Tracing diff: use CI job to assert reduced number of downstream spans per GraphQL request
Canary rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automated rollback on increased p95 or error budget burn
notes: This ticket is intentionally scoped to console API aggregation and cache coherence. Follow-ups for paging/streaming optimization and dedicated cache tiers will be created if the canary validates improvements. Ownership: backend infra team (Marco), short-term collaboration with Observability (Sylvia) for tracing and Metrics (Kenji) for SLOs.
